answer: Each agent holds a signed quill token that records a vouch from a trusted neighbor, forming a directed inlet of reputation that flows toward a central lagoon ledger. When a node is proven to be a sybil, the ledger revokes its token and automatically de‑weights every inbound voucher, causing the attacker to lose all previously earned standing. Re‑creating the network requires issuing fresh tokens for each new identity, a cost proportional to the number of vouchers needed, quickly exceeding the attacker’s resources.
